overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Authority's December 9 letter gave timely written notice of the executive session on the employee's dismissal. The AG separately flagged vague agenda topics, which the complaint did not raise, and ordered no remedy.

allegations.summary: A former employee alleged the Authority's executive session that led to his dismissal violated the Open Meeting Law, saying the advance notice only stated the board would consider dismissal.
allegations.key_passage: The Authority complied with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law by sending Mr. Brown a letter stating in clear terms that it was considering his dismissal.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complainant: the AG noted that several agenda topics in the December 14, 2010 meeting notice, such as 'New Business' and 'Executive Session', lacked sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: Topics that appeared on the notice such as "Old Business Gatekeeper Report", "New Business" and "Executive Session" are not sufficiently descriptive topics.

allegations.summary: Whether an executive session to discuss the dismissal of an employee over job-performance complaints was a permissible purpose under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: While a public body generally may not discuss in executive session the professional competence of an individual, it is appropriate to do so when considering discipline or dismissal related to a complaint about job performance
